thread:
lee: quick heads-up: onboarding canary for eve13b (int6 hybrid) is hitting OOMs on long sessions. repro with microbatch=4 + max_new_tokens=1024. short sessions fine. anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: saw it on node gpu-staging-07. snippet: ```RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.08 GiB (GPU 0; 80.0 GiB total, 76.9 GiB already allocated)
 at serve/gen.py:189```

kai: likely cause: int6 prefetch path creates extra KV stripe per microbatch and our slot allocator doesn't compact until end of request. microbatch 4 multiplies transient peak. two quick mitigations: cap microbatch at 1 for requests where ctx+req > 3k tokens OR reduce default max_new_tokens to 512 for eve13b. also kernel option streamed_attn reduces peak ~1.2GiB.

nora: I ran a 500-request bench with three configs: (A) fp16 baseline, (B) int6 default, (C) int6 with fp_head_layers=0-2 + streamed_attn + microbatch=1. Results: OOMs A:0/500 B:18/500 C:1/500. Long prompt perplexity A:20.1 B:22.3 C:20.6. Latency P95: A:210ms B:198ms C:205ms.

infra-bot: canary 3250001111-deploy -> staging nodes gpu-staging-05/07 with config microbatch=1,max_new_tokens=512,kernel=streamed_attn,fp_head_layers=0-2.

lee: consensus seems to be fp-head + streamed_attn + microbatch=1 as safe default for eve13b. action items: eng-runtime add session heuristic to auto-enforce microbatch=1 when requested_total_tokens>3000 (kai), eng-eval schedule ngram/regression sampling (nora), infra to run 2k synthetic requests after patch (sam). i'll update model onboarding notes and defaults.
